etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Origin uncertain. Either from gull (“to dupe, trick, fool”) +‎ -ible; or alternatively from Middle English gole, goll, gol (“an unfledged bird, silly fellow”), perhaps from Old Norse gulr (“yellow, pale”), from the hue of its down.
senses: Easily deceived or duped; naive, easily cheated or fooled.
A gullible person; someone easily fooled or tricked.
